title: A Real-Data Digital Twin Foundation for Battery-Electric Rail Vehicle Li-Ion Packs: Capacity-Fade and Equivalent-Circuit Identification on the NASA PCoE Dataset
content: Battery-electric rail vehicles (BERVs) need digital twins whose building blocks are identified from measured data before any prognostic or scenario layer is trusted. This study identifies the two foundational sub-models of a Li-ion digital twin from the NASA Ames Prognostics Center of Excellence (PCoE) dataset (cells B0005, B0006, B0007 and B0018): a power-law capacity-fade model and a first-order Thévenin equivalent-circuit model (ECM). Both were fitted by nonlinear least squares to measured data, with no synthetic data. The fade model explained 95.4–97.8% of the capacity variance (R2 = 0.954–0.978; RMSE = 24.5–37.1 mAh). The ECM reproduced one mid-life discharge voltage trace of cell B0005 with R2 = 0.936 (RMSE = 58.6 mV), but the series and polarisation resistances could not be separated: their standard errors exceeded the estimates, which matters for on-board parameter estimation in a rail battery management system. The fit also degrades at the discharge knee and in the post-discharge rest period. Finally, we specify, a vibration-coupled ageing law in which a stress multiplier derived from IEC 61373-type vibration spectra scales the capacity-loss rate. Its coupling coefficient needs vibration-instrumented cycling data that are not yet available.
